candidates.title: replace_memory_range keeps the inner nodes of a supplied dense hash tree: mark_pages_dirty (and the automatic all-dirty marking when a tree file is missing) recomputes only page hashes once the machine has been hashed, so a range's node hash, the root, proofs and a later snapshot can disagree with the contents
candidates.component: Emulator core: hash tree (src/hash-tree.cpp), memory_address_range, machine::replace_memory_range (C cm_replace_memory_range, Lua machine:replace_memory_range, JSON-RPC machine.replace_memory_range)
candidates.role: Hash tree: honest operator. The entry point (replace_memory_range) is part of 'the rest of the machine API'; no production PRT path is known to call it (inputs arrive through cmio), so it is rated as an off-path API operation, with the on-path rating given as the alternative.
candidates.location: src/hash-tree.cpp: hash_tree::return_updated_dirty_pages lines 381-394 ('if (changed || m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages) ... else mark_clean_page_and_up'), hash_tree::update lines 758-771 (flag cleared after the first successful update), hash-tree.hpp line 255; src/memory-address-range.cpp lines 72-79 (mark_pages_dirty / missing tree file only calls m_dpt.mark_dirty(), the mapped .dht is kept); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp machine_address_ranges::replace lines 662-686 (comment 'This will automatically start with all pages dirty'); src/machine.cpp machine::replace_memory_range lines 722-778; manual doc/README.md lines 3299-3310 and src/cartesi-machine.lua lines 276-279 (promise of mark_pages_dirty).
candidates.description: A page whose recomputed hash equals the leaf already stored in its dense hash tree is treated as 'marked dirty but not in fact dirty': hash_tree::return_updated_dirty_pages marks it clean and does not queue its address range for update_dense_trees, unless m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages is set. That flag is true only until the first successful hash_tree::update of the process (and after a failed one). This shortcut is sound only if every inner node of the dense tree is already consistent with its leaves. A range brought in by replace_memory_range gets a new memory_address_range that maps the caller-supplied .dht file as is; when backing_store.mark_pages_dirty is true, or when either tree file is omitted, the constructor only calls m_dpt.mark_dirty() and neither clears the dense tree nor asks the hash tree to bubble up. So on a machine that has already been hashed once, the 'forced recomputation' recomputes the page hashes, finds every page whose supplied leaf was right 'unchanged', cleans it, and leaves every inner node of the supplied file (including the range's root, which update_sparse_tree then copies into the sparse tree) untouched. The machine root hash, get_node_hash, get_proof, logs and claims computed by that process then do not correspond to the contents, verify_hash_tree() returns true, and the wrong nodes stay for good because the pages are now clean. The same supplied files give the correct root when used at machine creation or load (the flag is still true there), so the outcome of the documented knob depends on a hidden in-process flag. In the variant where only a .dht is supplied (no .dpt, which the manual says makes the emulator mark all pages dirty automatically), a later store() writes the wrong dense tree with clean dirty flags and mark_pages_dirty=false, so the emulator-written snapshot reloads with a cached root that differs from the root rebuilt from its contents. Stale but internally consistent trees (the emulator's own, for an older version of the image) are handled correctly; the defect needs a supplied dense tree whose inner nodes are not the hashes of its leaves (a tree file from a third-party image distributor, a damaged file, or one left by an interrupted update).
candidates.trigger: The trusted caller, with data from another party: it calls machine:replace_memory_range{start,length,backing_store={data_filename, dht_filename[, dpt_filename], mark_pages_dirty=true}} (or omits dpt_filename) on a machine whose hash tree was already updated (any earlier get_root_hash/get_proof/log/collect call), passing a range image and tree file it did not produce and relying on the documented recomputation. An image distributor chooses the .dht: correct page-level leaves, arbitrary inner nodes (it can set the range's node hash to any value, e.g. the node hash of a different, expected image).
candidates.reachability: Reached through a documented API with documented options; no fault injection and no guest involvement. Not reachable from the PRT honest path as far as I can see (crisium/prt.lua never call replace_memory_range; Dave/rollups node sources are out of scope). The cartesi-machine CLI replaces ranges before the first hash update of the process, where the flag is still true, so its usual flows are not affected; library, Lua and JSON-RPC callers that hash first (e.g. check the template hash, then replace drives, as the manual's template instantiation describes) are.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Trigger checked, not symptom. Not 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented': the API does not perform as documented (manual 3306-3308: 'Setting backing_store.mark_pages_dirty to true forces all pages to be marked dirty even when both tree files exist, so their hashes are recomputed on the next hash-tree update'; 'Otherwise, it marks all pages dirty'). The exclusion 'Defects that need the cached hash-tree data of a stored machine the operator did not produce to survive its adoption without a rebuild (O1)' does not fit on the preferred reading: the caller asked for the documented per-range rebuild and the supplied data survived it, and section 5 says 'A defect that defeats the rebuild itself ... is not excused by them'. Alternative reading: O1 only names the rebuild at load (clear_hash_tree), which still works here (machine:clear_hash_tree() after the replace gives the right root), and a supplied tree file is trusted caller data; then this is 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller' (Low).
rating_steps.2_role: The hash tree plays the honest-operator role ('the hash tree and its node proofs'). The entry point is in 'The rest of the machine API ... Honest operator where a production validator node plausibly calls it on the honest operator's path. When unsure, give both ratings.' I found no production path that replaces ranges, so: off-path (preferred), on-path (alternative).
rating_steps.3_high_medium: Matches the Medium case 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9).' (hash tree inconsistent in the running process in both variants; stored directory inconsistent in the dht-only variant).
rating_steps.4_critical: Only if a production node calls replace_memory_range with supplied tree files on the honest operator's path: R9 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents. This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash, after any sequence of documented operations ... and every snapshot the emulator itself writes.'
rating_steps.5_low: Low under the alternative reading of step 1 (supplied tree files are trusted caller data and only clear_hash_tree is a rebuild).

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: off-path machine API operation that leaves the hash tree and, in the dht-only variant, a stored directory inconsistent with the contents, R9) / Critical if a production node replaces ranges with supplied tree files on the honest operator's path / Low if supplied tree files count as trusted caller data
candidates.threat_to_goal: Not a direct break of the section 1 goal on the PRT path found. It violates R9 and the manual: after documented operations the root, node hashes and proofs of the machine do not describe its contents, the tool meant to check this (verify_hash_tree) reports success, and one variant writes a snapshot with a wrong cached root. An operator that instantiates a template by replacing drives with third-party images plus their tree files, and relies on mark_pages_dirty as the manual states, would defend (or accept as matching an expected hash) a state hash that its contents do not have: a completeness failure of the kind 'The honest operator computes a wrong hash'.
candidates.evidence: Ran with the in-tree build (. bugs/env.sh), scripts kept in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r5/INVHASH/: t_replace.lua (modes 'mark' and 'nodpt'), t_replace2.lua, t_replace3.lua. Setup: machine with a flash drive at 0x80000000000000 of 8 pages (image A), get_root_hash once; replacement image B; .dht taken from the emulator's own store of a machine holding B, with only inner nodes changed (leaves kept). Results: (1) mark_pages_dirty=true with dht+dpt: root 3822f18d... vs fresh machine with the same contents ff90e966...; verify_hash_tree()=true; after machine:clear_hash_tree() the root becomes ff90e966...; the same backing_store at machine creation gives ff90e966... (2) dht only, no dpt (automatic all-dirty): same wrong root. (3) Replacing only the root slot of the .dht by 0x4242...42: get_node_hash(range start, 15) returns 0x4242...42 after the 'forced recomputation', the machine root is wrong, and it stays wrong after later updates. (4) Persistence: with explicit mark_pages_dirty=true, store() records mark_pages_dirty=true for the range and a reload rebuilds it (heals); in the dht-only variant, store(dir, SHARING_ALL) writes a snapshot whose cached root differs from the root of the same directory loaded with clear_hash_tree=true (cached root == rebuilt root: false), i.e. the wrong node is in the emulator-written snapshot. (5) Control: an emulator-written, internally consistent but stale .dht (image changed in one page outside the emulator) plus mark_pages_dirty=true gives the correct root. No sanitizer report under the ASan/UBSan build.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua (deterministic, a few seconds): create machine M with one 8-page flash drive (image A) and call M:get_root_hash(). Build image B; obtain B's .dht/.dpt by storing a scratch machine that holds B; overwrite the inner nodes (bytes 32..255 of the 512-byte .dht, leaves at 256..511 kept). Call M:replace_memory_range{start,length,backing_store={data_filename=B, dht_filename=crafted, dpt_filename=dpt, mark_pages_dirty=true}} and, in a second machine, the same without dpt_filename and mark_pages_dirty. Required (R9 and manual 3306-3310): M:get_root_hash() equals the root of a fresh machine created with image B (equivalently the root after M:clear_hash_tree()), and for the dht-only variant the root of M:store(dir) loaded without clear_hash_tree equals the root of the same directory loaded with clear_hash_tree=true. Today both assertions fail (exit 1); they pass once the replaced range is fully rebuilt (e.g. clear the mapped dense tree whenever all pages are force-marked dirty, or make the hash tree bubble up the range after a replace).

not_covered: No second candidate: the rest of the inventory (below) found the code consistent. Files read in full: hash-tree.cpp/.hpp, page-hash-tree-cache.hpp, dense-hash-tree.hpp, dirty-page-tree.hpp, i-dense-hash-tree.hpp, i-dirty-page-tree.hpp, back-merkle-tree.cpp/.hpp, hash-tree-proof.hpp, i-hasher.hpp, simd-hasher.hpp, variant-hasher.hpp, keccak-256-hasher.cpp/.hpp, is-pristine.cpp/.hpp, hash-tree-hash.cpp, the proof/node/update/store/collect parts of machine.cpp, collect-*-state-access.hpp, uarch-record-state-access.hpp, record-send-cmio-state-access.hpp. complete-merkle-tree and pristine-merkle-tree do not exist on this branch.

Inventory items judged unreachable or harmless, not reported: release-build null dereference behind 'assert(opt_br)' in get_page_proof/get_dense_node_hash/update_page (needs every cache entry borrowed, i.e. a leak after an exception: the known R3-VARDIRTY family); entry_payload::node_hash_view accepts index == start ('index > start', an out-of-bounds read for offset 4096) but every caller masks the offset below the page size; get_page_proof/get_dense_node_hash store a recomputed page hash in the dense tree without bubbling up when they miss the cache on a page that differs from its leaf (only possible if the skip_hash_tree_update callers run on a stale tree, which I could not produce); update_dense_trees skips ranges with 'level > level_count' instead of '>=' (the extra level is an empty view); writes of junk parents into the process-global no_hash scratch in update_words (R1-R9-2, dropped earlier); simd_*_hasher's function-local static optimal_queue_size is fixed by the first hash function used in the process (performance only).

Dynamic checks done, all consistent (no candidate): incremental root/proofs vs fresh rebuild under random write_memory (4 machines with concurrency 1/2/4 and phtc_size 1/3/16/4096, non-power-of-two RAM and flash); large dirty sets with 1-4 OpenMP threads; collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes (update_words path) vs run_uarch+get_root_hash per uarch cycle with phtc_size 1 and 2 on a Linux boot; a shared stored machine (SHARING_ALL) driven by random run / write_memory / collect_* / log_step_uarch / log_reset_uarch / clear_hash_tree / store, then destroyed and reloaded: cached root, node hashes and word/page proofs equal those after clear_hash_tree (6 seeds, about 200 reloads, phtc_size 1-300); keccak256 and sha256 scalar paths vs cast/hashlib at block-boundary lengths; ASan/UBSan runs of the same scripts. Not done: runs on AVX-512 or non-x86 hosts (only the dispatch selected on this host was executed), 16-lane SHA-256 paths, big-endian (rejected at compile time).

Crash/power-loss consistency of the shared .dht/.dpt/.sht/.phtc files (the phtc initialized-tag protocol, msync ordering) was only read; O2 excludes reloading such directories. fsync error handling and the Windows / non-mmap fallback paths of os::mapped_memory were only skimmed.

Exceptions inside hash_tree::update, update_words (pmr allocations between a leaf write and its bubbling) and inside OpenMP regions were not fault-injected (R1-O2-3 / R3-VARDIRTY-1 family already confirmed).
JSON-RPC server: fork with OpenMP paused, fork_server, rebind, and concurrent use of several machines in one process from different threads (process-global scratch and statics) were not exercised.
SHA-256 machines were only used for hashing checks; proofs and persistence under sha256 were not swept (no referee verifier supports it).

back_merkle_tree was checked by hand-tracing push_back/pad_back/get_context on small cases and by reading its callers; no randomized differential against a naive tree was run. The Lua cartesi.hash-tree frontier/forest helpers (support, R4-RGPROOF-1 pending) were not examined.
Worst-case cost of one hash-tree update against the dispute clocks (R12) was not measured; only read for super-linear behavior (none found beyond R1-R8-3 and R1-O1-2).
replace_memory_range followed by store with SHARING_NONE/CONFIG, and replacement ranges with shared backing stores (R3-VARCACHE-1 area), were not re-tested beyond the candidate's own experiments.
Whether any production validator node (out of scope here) calls replace_memory_range with supplied tree files on the honest path, which decides the candidate's role.
